verses.text: David gathered Israel's chosen men again, thirty thousand in all.
He and everyone with him set out from Baale Judah to bring back God's ark. It bears the name of the LORD of Armies, who sits enthroned above the cherubim.
They put God's ark on a new cart and brought it out of Abinadab's house on the hill. His sons Uzzah and Ahio drove the cart.
They brought God's ark out from the house on the hill, and Ahio walked ahead of it.
David and all Israel made music before the LORD with every kind of cypress-wood instrument, including harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals.
When they reached Nacon's threshing floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and grabbed God's ark.
The LORD was furious with Uzzah. God struck him there for what he had done, and he died beside the ark.
David was upset because the LORD had struck Uzzah. He named the place Perez Uzzah, and it still goes by that name.
David was afraid of the LORD that day. “How can I bring the LORD's ark to my city?” he asked.
So David decided against taking the ark into David's City. He took it to the home of Obed-Edom from Gath instead.
The LORD's ark stayed with Obed-Edom from Gath for three months, and the LORD blessed him and his whole household.
Word reached King David that the LORD had blessed Obed-Edom's household and everything he owned because of God's ark. So David went to get the ark and brought it into David's City with joy.
After the people carrying the LORD's ark had gone six steps, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
David wore a linen ephod and danced before the LORD with all his strength.
David and all Israel brought up the LORD's ark with loud cheers and the blast of a trumpet.
As the ark entered David's City, Saul's daughter Michal looked out the window. She saw King David jumping and dancing before the LORD and felt nothing but contempt for him.
They brought in the LORD's ark and set it in the middle of the tent David had put up for it. David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
After presenting the offerings, David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Armies.
He gave every man and woman in the crowd of Israelites a portion of bread, dates, and raisins. Then everyone went home.

When David came home to bless his household, Saul's daughter Michal came out to meet him. “How dignified the king of Israel looked today, exposing himself in front of his servants' maids like a shameless fool!”
David answered Michal, “I was dancing before the LORD, who chose me over your father and his entire family to lead Israel, his people. I'll keep celebrating before the LORD.
I'll make an even bigger fool of myself and think nothing of my own status. But those maids you just mentioned will honor me.”
Saul's daughter Michal never had a child.
